questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

__Had I__ a rich person, I would share my wealth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Were I**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the underlined segment, the use of the past tense verb 'Had' is **in**correct.
 
• "**Had I**" is **past indicative**, denoting a mood of the verb expressing a simple statement of a fact.
 
• While "**Were I**" is **past subjunctive**. The subjunctive mood is used when we are expressing something counterfactual, usually when we’re expressing doubt or a wish.
 
• We use **'were' with 'I'** when we **express imagination or wish**.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct Sentence__: ***Were I **a rich person, I would share my wealth*.

Sh! Someone listens to our conversation.
questions.solution:

• In the given sentence, the use of the third-person singular present form of the verb 'listens' is incorrect.
 
• The given sentence is in the present continuous tense. 
 
• We use the present continuous tense when **an action or condition is happening now, frequently, and may continue into the future**.
 
• The Present Continuous Formula: to be (**am, is, are**) + verb (**the present participle**).
 
• The present continuous form of the verb "is listening" should be used in place of "listens".

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct Sentence__**: ***Sh! Someone **is listening to** our conversation*.

questions.question: **According to the passage, we visit zoos ______.**

options.text: to watch the frustration of animals in cages
to see how animals behave in zoos
to spend a day out for fun and excitement
to see the animals in cages

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**to spend a day out for fun and excitement**'.
